title: LIV Golf vendors report unpaid invoices as Saudi PIF funding ends this month
dek: LIV Golf vendors and contractors report unpaid invoices ranging from thousands to nearly $100,000 as the league's Saudi PIF funding ends this month and LIV pursues new investment. The league has filed a WARN Act notice signaling potential mass layoffs and is exploring a funding deal with BC Partners' credit division.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: LIV Golf vendors report unpaid invoices ranging from thousands to nearly $100,000, per Front Office Sports reporting.
bottom_line: Watch for whether BC Partners completes a funding commitment and on what terms, and whether vendor payments resume once new capital arrives. If the league files for bankruptcy protection or if major player contracts (Jon Rahm is reportedly owed more than $100 million) become subject to restructuring, LIV's ability to operate a full 2027 schedule would be invalidated.
body: Vendors and contractors working with LIV Golf report unpaid invoices ranging from thousands to nearly $100,000 as the league's Saudi Public Investment Fund announced in April it would no longer fund LIV after the 2026 season, according to reporting from Front Office Sports.

The unpaid amounts come as LIV seeks new investment to continue operating. Communication from LIV regarding the money owed has been minimal, per the reporting. One contractor stated: "There's no response from the accounts receivable department. Even their legal counsel has not responded to demand letters."

Canadian technology company Mobii Systems Group Limited, which previously supplied LIV's "Any Shot, Any Time" streaming option, sued the league last month claiming LIV owes it more than $1.1 million for breach of contract, unpaid invoices, and interest. No full-time employees are known to have seen missed paychecks since the PIF announced in April it would no longer fund LIV after this season, suggesting the league is prioritizing employee payroll over vendor payments.

LIV has outsourced services including video production, data collection, merchandising, and tournament food and beverage operations, creating an extended network of vendors now navigating payment delays. The league filed a Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act notice last month, a legal requirement for U.S. businesses with more than 100 employees to provide at least 60 days notice of potential mass layoffs. Earlier this month the league began giving some contractors 30-day termination notices effective in early September, with language referencing potential opportunities in a "LIV 2.0 structure."

Joe Bain, co-chair of law firm Jones Walker's bankruptcy and restructuring team in Houston, stated that withholding payments to outside entities is "absolutely" a strategy companies use when preparing for potential bankruptcy filing. Corporate restructuring experts Gene Davis and Jon Zinman are leading LIV's new independent board of directors.

BC Partners' credit division is exploring a funding deal with LIV to help the league continue operating in 2027 and beyond. The PIF has spent more than $5 billion on LIV since the league launched in 2022. LIV CEO Scott O'Neil said this month that the PIF "has been a tremendous steward of this business" and expressed appreciation for their willingness to allow the league time to find new investment. Terms of the PIF's exit as LIV's lead financial backer remain unclear from the available source text. The specific timeline and terms for BC Partners' proposed funding deal have not been disclosed.
